title: Converging Arc Lat Pulldown
summary: A plate-loaded pulldown whose arms travel in a converging arc, matching the line of the lat fibres and loading the lats hard at the top stretch.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.45 for upper back (helper): each working set adds 0.45 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.4 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.3 for traps (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.25 for rear delts (minor): each working set adds 0.25 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.

setup.text: Sit with your thighs under the pad and reach up for the handles, letting your shoulders rise.
Pull down and in until your elbows are at your sides.
Return slowly all the way to the top stretch.

form_cues.cue: Pull the handles in an arc toward your hips
The heaviest part is near the top. Don't cut the stretch short.

mistakes.text: Rocking the torso to start the rep.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Lat width focus, Steadier cable tension.
Swap sheet: One side at a time, Steadier cable tension.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stretch emphasis, Less stable, Lower loading potential.
